decisions.reason: As a core drainage component with its own pages in both 2018 and 2019, it still looks like a viable option whose carrying cost is likely modest within the firm's modular product architecture, even if it is not the clearest strategic focus.
A floor-level shower drainage system fits the firm's stated direction very closely, so despite remaining uncertainty, the option value of keeping it is high relative to its likely incremental cost.

Because management presented this designer shower drainage line as a flagship and it matches the move toward design-conscious integrated bathroom solutions, it is unlikely to be withdrawn absent clear failure evidence.

The integrated-slope shower element supports installation ease and renovation use cases central to the firm's strategy, so management would likely keep it as a complementary option unless demand has clearly disappointed.
Its prominent launch and homepage visibility suggest meaningful market relevance, and the product extends the firm's drainage expertise into a defensible adjacent niche with continued option value.

Since it was only mentioned rather than strongly promoted and sits somewhat farther from the firm's main shower-drainage trajectory, management is more likely to reallocate resources away from this weaker option.
